item: California estate, inheritance or gift tax on a death today
value: None
source_title: State Controller's Office — California Estate Tax
evidence: 'For decedents that die on or after January 1, 2005, there is no longer a requirement to file a California Estate Tax Return.' Inheritance tax is collected only for deaths before June 8, 1982.

item: Which transfers are excluded from reassessment
value: Family home: principal residence of the parent that becomes the principal residence of the child. Other real property: no exclusion.
evidence: Chart, Prop 19 column: 'Principal residence of transferor and transferee'; 'Value limit of current taxable value plus $1,000,000 (as biennially adjusted)'; 'Eliminates exclusion for other real property other than the principal residence'.

item: The $1 million allowance for transfers Feb 16, 2025 – Feb 15, 2027
evidence: 'for transfers that occur February 16, 2025 through February 15, 2027, the value cap will be the sum of the property's factored base year value plus $1,044,586.' Earlier amounts: $1,000,000 (2021–23), $1,022,600 (2023–25).

item: How the $1 million allowance is adjusted
value: Every other February 16, by the FHFA California House Price Index change for the prior calendar year only (2024: 2.15%)
evidence: 'every other February 16 thereafter... adjust the one million dollar amount... to reflect the percentage change in the House Price Index for California for the prior calendar year'. 'The next adjustment ... will occur in February 2027.' One year of price change is applied every two years, so the allowance grows at roughly half the pace of home prices.

value: Factored base year value immediately before the transfer + the adjusted $1 million
evidence: 'Excluded Amount — the factored base year value ... immediately prior to the date of transfer, plus $1 million... Also known as the "value cap."' 'Excess Amount — the full cash value ... on the date of transfer minus the "excluded amount."'

item: New taxable value when market value exceeds the value cap
value: Factored base year value + excess amount (equivalently: market value − adjusted $1 million)
evidence: 'If the full cash value on the date of transfer exceeds the value cap, the amount above the value cap is added to the factored base year value, resulting in a new taxable value. A new taxable value is to be annually adjusted by an inflation factor'.

value: The home must become the heir's principal residence within one year after the transfer; no exceptions
evidence: 'the transfer is required to be of a principal residence of the transferor that qualifies as the principal residence of the transferee within one year after the transfer ... There are no exceptions to this rule.'

value: Homeowners' Exemption claim within 1 year of the transfer; exclusion claim within 3 years or before a sale to a third party, whichever is earlier
evidence: 'the transferee must file for the Homeowners' ... Exemption within one year of the date of purchase or transfer... must also file for the appropriate intergenerational transfer exclusion within three years ... or before a transfer to a third party, whichever is earlier.' A claim is also timely within six months of a supplemental or escape assessment notice. Late claims: prospective relief only.

item: If the heir later moves out or rents the home
value: Exclusion is removed; assessed value becomes the date-of-death market value, increased by the annual inflation factor, from the next lien date
source_title: BOE Letter to Assessors 2026/026, 'Continual Use Requirement' and Q8
evidence: 'The value to be enrolled on the lien date following the date the exclusion no longer qualifies is the full cash value established as of the change in ownership date (new base year value), adjusted annually for inflation'. Q8: for a sole claimant who moves out 'the exclusion shall be removed'; moving back in does not restore it.

item: If the heir never moves in (rents it out or leaves it empty)
value: Reassessed to full market value as of the date of transfer
evidence: 'if the qualifying child does not occupy the parent's ... principal residence, it will be ineligible for the intergenerational transfer exclusion and will be reassessed to its full cash value as of the date of purchase or transfer.'

item: Transfers through a trust at death
value: Covered: a 'transfer' includes transfers due to death, within or outside a trust
evidence: 'Transfer — any transfer of the present beneficial ownership of a family home ... between a parent and a child... This includes transfers occurring between the living and those occurring due to death, whether within or outside a trust.'

value: Only one home can be the heir's principal residence
evidence: 'only one can qualify as the child's principal residence and thus qualify for the intergenerational transfer exclusion.' The heir cannot keep a principal residence in San Francisco and claim the exclusion in Cupertino.

value: Only the unit the parent occupied as a principal residence can qualify
evidence: 'only the unit occupied as the principal residence qualifies ... The remainder ... would be reassessed at its full cash value as of the date of transfer.' Not relevant to the Cupertino single-family home; noted for completeness.

value: Lesser of California CPI change or 2% per year
evidence: 'Revenue and Taxation Code section 51 provides that base year values ... shall be compounded annually by an inflation factor, not to exceed 2 percent.'

value: 1.02 (California CPI change 3.307%)
evidence: 'please prepare your 2026 assessment roll using an inflation factor of 1.02.' Measured August 2024 to August 2025 because no October 2025 index was issued.

Enclosed table of final factors 1976-77 to 2026-27. The year-over-year changes in the owner-supplied assessed-value histories (about +0.5%, +2%, +1.5%, +2% x4, +1%, +2% x5) match these factors year for year.

item: How often the factor has been below 2% (1976-77 to 2026-27)

value: $7,000 off taxable value for an owner-occupied principal residence as of January 1
evidence: 'The California Constitution provides a $7,000 reduction in the taxable value for a qualifying owner-occupied home. The home must have been the principal place of residence of the owner on the lien date, January 1st.' Form BOE-266, one-time filing; by February 15 for the full exemption.

item: Change-in-ownership statement when property passes at death through a trust
value: Filed by the trustee within 150 days after the date of death
evidence: 'including a transfer through the medium of a trust, the change in ownership statement ... shall be filed by the trustee (if the property was held in trust) or the transferee ... within 150 days after the date of death.'

item: Trustee's notice when a revocable trust becomes irrevocable at death
value: Served within 60 days on each beneficiary and each heir
evidence: (a)(1) notice required 'When a revocable trust ... becomes irrevocable because of the death of one or more of the settlors'; (f) 'not later than 60 days following the occurrence of the event'.

evidence: 'Annual rent increases are capped at "5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living," up to a maximum of 10%... apply to most rental housing in California that is more than 15 years old, including single-family homes and condos owned by corporations'.
